prior_lines.scope: BTC 5m triple-barrier oracle-label entry axis: TB-transformer (12-run seed/hygiene sweep), 60-asset panel pooling and asset selection, naive direction baselines, event-sampler effective-sample-size fix
prior_lines.reason: The shipped checkpoint's headline OOS number (35.5% win rate/-9.5% sum_ret) was the luckiest of 12 retrains (3 seeds x 4 hygiene variants): pooled gross edge -0.29bps, 0/12 OOS-positive, and it loses to an always_short baseline. 60-asset x 5-seed panel pooling (300 runs) had negative capture in every ceiling tercile with VAL-vs-OOS capture rank correlation of only 0.061, so asset selection cannot rescue it either. Event/importance sampling cannot raise effective sample size above the uniform-stride baseline (it only shrinks it further). Capacity-reduction sweep RETESTED 2026-08-07 (`scripts/g5_btc_tb_entry_capacity_reduction_20260807.py`, XGBoost depth in {1,3,4,8,12,16}, N=5 seeds each, same purge+uniqueness hygiene): VAL-selected ranking and OOS-selected ranking of the 6 capacity levels are essentially uncorrelated (best-by-VAL is depth=1; best-by-OOS is depth=8-12, worst-by-VAL) -- the same VAL/OOS capture-decorrelation pattern G4c already found for asset selection (rho=0.061), now reproduced for the capacity axis. No capacity level clears the always_short bar on the only legitimate (VAL) selection signal, so this does not reopen the entry axis; treat the depth=8-12 OOS numbers as a multiple-comparisons artifact, not a validated finding.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Any future entry-axis claim on this label must report N>=5 genuinely random seeds (not a single run) plus purge+embargo+uniqueness weighting (label spans overlap heavily: effective_n ~4,058 vs 43,798 nominal) before it can be trusted, AND must select any hyperparameter/capacity/asset choice on VAL only, confirming on OOS exactly once -- this line has now independently reproduced VAL/OOS selection decorrelation twice (asset choice, capacity choice). A materially different feature set never included in the causalfix_final 113-column panel used here is the strongest remaining differentiator; a capacity sweep alone is not, since this retest already covered depth 1-16 without a VAL-legitimate winner.

prior_lines.scope: BTC 5m exit/risk layer keyed to zigzag pivot timing: perfect-foresight pivot-exit ceiling, a pivot-nowcast classifier (3-class, AUC 0.90-0.95 OOS) turned into an exit rule, and full/partial/scaled marginal-EV exit primitives derived from it
prior_lines.reason: The perfect-pivot-exit ceiling is real and large (VAL +39.0%/OOS +59.9% resimulated) but only realizable at <=3-bar lead time -- by lead time k=6 it is already negative. The nowcast classifier generalizes cleanly (7-20x precision lift over base rate) yet captures ~0 of the ceiling (recall 2.5-14.5%). Marginal-EV analysis found the classifier's own high-confidence bucket has the MOST negative marginal EV on both splits (worst bucket OOS -39.63bps, t=-2.39). RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (`scripts/p3_btc_exit_marginal_ev_true_positive_decomposition_20260807.py`, N=5 seeds, same k=1 nowcaster): decomposed by ground-truth true/false positive. Marginal EV restricted to TRUE adverse-pivot bars is strongly POSITIVE in every probability bucket, both splits (t=2.2-8.2, e.g. OOS [0.2,0.35): +63.8bps t=5.7) -- profitable pivots are NOT structurally undetectable, contrary to the earlier open question. The negative pooled result is fully explained by precision: false positives outnumber true positives at every threshold (best bucket OOS precision 25.9% vs 35.5% needed to break even), and false-positive marginal EV gets MORE negative as the classifier's confidence rises (0bps -> -150bps OOS). BUT: the one bucket/split cell where actual precision clears its breakeven point (VAL [0.1,0.2): 15.9% actual vs 11.7% breakeven, pooled +3.37bps) does NOT replicate OOS (12.65% actual vs 19.8% breakeven, pooled -4.65bps) -- a third independent reproduction of this repo's VAL/OOS selection-decorrelation pattern (after G4c's asset selection and the capacity-reduction sweep). No operating point is yet shown to reliably monetize this out-of-sample.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: The mechanism is understood (precision, not EV sign) but THREE follow-up fixes all FAILED to survive out-of-sample confirmation 2026-08-07, N=5 seed-averaged each, all VAL-selected then confirmed once: (1) `p4_..._multihorizon_gate` (k=1 AND k=2 agreement) -- best VAL-eligible ~0.0pp lift. (2) `p5_..._persistence_filter` (probability sustained >=m consecutive bars) -- best VAL-eligible -4.07pp. (3) `p6_..._two_stage_precision_classifier` (a genuine second-stage XGBoost, no-leakage stacked on stage-1's out-of-fold probabilities + causal features, candidate-zone-restricted) -- this one DID clear VAL (+3.22pp, 46 trades) and even agreed on the already-spent Jan-Mar OOS (+5.41pp, 63 trades), but the single confirmation on the genuinely untouched 2026-04-01..08-01 window REVERSED it: -4.06pp, 41 trades (a real sample, not noise). This is the FOURTH independent reproduction of this repo's VAL/OOS(and now VAL/OOS-agreeing-but-still-wrong) selection-decorrelation pattern in one session (after G4c asset selection, the capacity-reduction sweep, and P3's bucket selection) -- and the strongest form of it, since even a second data point (already-spent OOS) agreeing with VAL was not sufficient. The fresh 2026-04-01..08-01 window is now fully spent for this research line; no further confirmation is possible without new data accumulating.
prior_lines.monetization_status: operationally closed as of 2026-08-07 -- the underlying true-positive signal (P3) is real, but no delivery mechanism (threshold/agreement/persistence/two-stage-classifier) has survived a clean confirmation. Do not resume without either (a) new data extending the untouched window, or (b) a fundamentally different exit representation, not another filter/classifier on the same k=1/k=2 nowcast outputs.

prior_lines.scope: ETH (plus BTC/SOL transfer checks) 5m entry/filter search across 17 independently falsification-audited ideas in one overnight session: conformal-prediction (APS) abstention on h48qual's own direction probabilities; path-signature features (time-return Levy area, price-volume Levy area); a 144-bar naive momentum rule; session/day-of-week calendar features; taker buy/sell order-flow imbalance; BTC lead-lag momentum; cross-sectional relative strength vs a BTC+SOL basket; six binary skip-filter feature families (momentum/OFI, realized-vol/ATR, combined, Hawkes self-exciting jump-clustering, Kaufman Efficiency Ratio, and a 44-feature kitchen-sink of all of them); a genuine two-model priority-router replica built after reading trading_bot_modules/omega4_6_1_live.py directly (PRIORITY=(h48qual,zig075), thresholds 0.50/0.75); and quantile-regression forward-return skew. Scripts scripts/research_*_20260809.py, per-idea writeups project-eth-*-20260809.md (memory), consolidated in docs/entry_exit_edge_root_cause_and_literature_review_20260809.md Part 4.
prior_lines.reason: All 17 negative. One (144-bar naive momentum) initially appeared to clear every gate (falsification_audit, VAL, and a partial OOS look, plus a BTC transfer check) but was RETRACTED the same night: ETH and BTC's tp_move:sl_move label ratio is fixed at 2.083:1 while realized barrier-touch outcomes split close to 1:1, so ANY consistent directional bet (including the two most information-free strategies possible, always_long and always_short) earns a large structural edge in this proxy independent of skill -- always_short alone beat the momentum rule on both VAL (welch_t=-8.85) and the partial OOS window (welch_t=-11.77) once benchmarked correctly, and was positive in 20-21 of 21 months on both assets despite ETH falling 49% over the period. The kitchen-sink combined model (44 features) had AUC 0.9564 in-sample vs 0.5166/0.5170 on DEV/VAL (n=17,855/35,136) on the raw win/loss target -- near-perfect memorization, no real out-of-sample generalization. The two-model priority-router replica, built to faithfully mirror the real live code's mechanism, was statistically a wash at h48qual's actual threshold (0.50) and negative at looser thresholds, showing h48qual's real blocking value depends on its actual feature/label engineering and cannot be replicated from generic technical features in a few hours.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Two reusable methodology artifacts came out of this line independent of the entry-search outcome, and apply to ANY future quick proxy backtest on this label family: (1) the baseline must be max(always_long, always_short) on the identical period and cost assumption, never a one-sample test against zero -- see project memory project-baseline-must-be-always-long-short-not-zero-20260809; (2) a 3-way reclassification model conflates 'skip a bad bar' (the one mechanism this repo has repeatedly shown can work, e.g. h48qual's blocking) with 're-pick the opposite direction' (never works here) -- use a binary skip-filter on a TRAIN-frozen favored direction instead for any future filter-style claim, and note that even that framing failed decisively here across 6 feature families including the full 44-feature combination. A genuinely new causal raw source (real order-book/L2 data, sentiment, or on-chain data not already covered by this repo's existing closed on-chain lines) is the strongest differentiator for reopening entry search on ETH/BTC/SOL 5m; another generic-technical-feature variant on locally available OHLCV-derived data is not, since momentum, order flow, cross-asset lead-lag and relative strength, realized volatility, jump-clustering, and trend-efficiency were all covered here, alone and in full combination, across three modeling paradigms (3-way classification, binary win-probability, quantile regression).

N=5 genuinely random seeds ([147360281, 303419845, 783674062, 809896406, 824654821]), expert=bull, plain CE, true 115-feature live pipeline, collapse diagnostic recorded every epoch (not just at the selected checkpoint) so true-peak-epoch diversity was measurable for the first time. Accuracy: both selected-checkpoint and true-peak direction_balanced_accuracy deltas vs r=1 have std exceeding |mean| by 1.6-14x and are sign-inconsistent across seeds (r=2: selected -0.0065+/-0.0106 1/5 improved, true-peak -0.0013+/-0.0109 2/5 improved; r=3: selected -0.0015+/-0.0078 1/5 improved, true-peak -0.0008+/-0.0111 2/5 improved) -- the tabm_hp_low_signal_pattern signature. Diversity (the mechanism the whole candidate targets): pairwise top-confidence correlation at the true-peak epoch is essentially unchanged, mean delta -0.00003 (r=2) / -0.00010 (r=3) across seeds, individual per-seed deltas randomly signed in +-0.0002-0.0007 -- rank-r measurably fails to increase ensemble diversity in this architecture/label/recipe combination, not merely due to a checkpoint-timing artifact (the single-seed cheap_gate's open question is now closed). Full detail: docs/experiments/eth_odyssey4_dl_reference_deep_analysis_20260816.md section 6 (6.1-6.8).
prior_lines.retest_guidance: This closes the capacity/init-based branch of BatchEnsemble-diversity fixes on this architecture (k-reduction, wider gate init std, and now rank-r generalization all independently failed to either help accuracy or demonstrably increase diversity). Do not retry another capacity or initialization variant of the same gate mechanism. The one qualitatively different, still-untested axis is an explicit diversity-promoting term added directly to the training loss (e.g. negative-correlation-learning-style penalty on inter-member logit correlation) rather than giving the gate more capacity -- that has not been tried. A competing, and arguably better-supported, hypothesis is that the collapse is downstream of the zigzag_action label's own non-causal pivot-confirmation structure (section 3.1: easy-majority bars solved by shallow momentum give every ensemble member the same easy signal to converge on) rather than the gate's expressiveness -- since diversity did not respond to strictly more gate capacity at all, a loss-side or label-side fix is the more promising next step, not another architecture-side one.

prior_lines.scope: Explicit Negative Correlation Learning (NCL) diversity-promoting term added directly to the canonical ThreeHeadTabM training loss (architecture completely unmodified), following Krogh & Vedelsby (1994, ambiguity decomposition), Liu & Yao (1999, doi:10.1016/s0893-6080(99)00073-8, NCL), and Wang/Chen/Yao (2010, doi:10.1109/ijcnn.2010.5596702, NCL for classification): total_loss = task_loss - lambda * ambiguity, where ambiguity = mean_batch[mean_k(||p_k - p_mean||^2)] on direction_head's per-member softmax probabilities. This was the one qualitatively different axis identified after the rank-r gate candidate (eth_odyssey4_rankr_batchensemble_gate_20260817) confirmed that giving the ensemble more architectural capacity does not by itself restore diversity -- this candidate instead forces diversity directly through the loss.
prior_lines.reason: Single-seed cheap_gate (scripts/research_eth_odyssey4_ncl_diversity_loss_cheap_gate_20260817.py) swept lambda across 9 points (0/1/2/3/5/7/10/100/1000) and found a smooth, monotonic dose-response, not a cliff: lambda<=3 barely moves diversity or accuracy; lambda=5 is the first point where both move together; lambda=7 is a sharp transition (accuracy 0.571->0.49-0.53, pairwise correlation 0.997->0.56); lambda>=10 stays broken on both axes. N=5 genuinely random seeds (scripts/research_eth_odyssey4_ncl_diversity_loss_nseed_confirm_20260817.py, seeds [121889256,241992079,411267114,631193301,951559053]) confirmed the two boundary points with a paired design (same seed/init per arm, lambda is the only difference): lambda=7 vs 0 is sign-consistent and robust on EVERY metric -- 5/5 seeds worse on both selected-checkpoint (-0.0534+/-0.0254) and true-peak (-0.0497+/-0.0076, std only 15% of the mean -- the least noise-confounded result in this entire research line) direction_balanced_accuracy, and 5/5 seeds show large diversity increase (true-peak pairwise correlation delta -0.513+/-0.110, mean corr 0.998->0.485). Diversity genuinely increased (unlike the rank-r candidate) but at a large, robust, non-noise accuracy cost. lambda=2 was NOT a reliably safe small value either: 3/5 seeds showed negligible correlation change but 2/5 seeds showed a large collapse-breaking correlation drop (-0.42, -0.41) similar in magnitude to lambda=7 -- whether a small lambda triggers the diversity-forcing regime is seed/init-trajectory-dependent, not a fixed threshold. No lambda in the tested range produced increased diversity without a comparable-or-worse accuracy cost. Full detail: docs/experiments/eth_odyssey4_dl_reference_deep_analysis_20260816.md section 7.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not retry this exact ambiguity-on-softmax-probability NCL formulation, nor a narrower lambda sweep in the tested 0-1000 range -- the dose-response is smooth and monotonic (confirmed at 9 points single-seed, 2 boundary points N=5-seed) with no free region found. This closes the SIXTH and final independently-tried mechanism for the ThreeHeadTabM BatchEnsemble collapse (k-reduction, quality-target separation, R-gate wide-init, lr isolation, rank-r gate generalization, and now an explicit loss-side diversity term) -- every capacity, initialization, and loss-side lever tried either fails to increase diversity at all (rank-r) or increases it only at a large, robust, confirmed cost to accuracy (this candidate). The two failure modes are opposite and mutually reinforcing: since diversity does not respond usefully to EITHER more architectural room to diverge OR direct loss-side pressure to diverge, the most strongly supported remaining hypothesis is that the collapse is downstream of the zigzag_action label's own non-causal pivot-confirmation structure (section 3.1: all 8 members converge on the same shallow momentum-following shortcut because that is what the label rewards), not a fixable property of the gate or loss. Any future revival of this general research line should target the label/feature side, not another architecture- or loss-side diversity mechanism on the same zigzag_action target.

prior_lines.scope: Information-driven bar sampling (Easley/Lopez de Prado/O'Hara Volume Clock DOI:10.3905/jpm.2012.39.1.019; AFML ch.2) as a controlled A/B against calendar 5m bars built from the SAME 1m ETHUSDT stream (2024-12..2026-03, data/training_features_1m.csv): dollar/volume/tick bars with TRAIN-only fixed thresholds (avg 5m-equivalent), identical 19-feature causal contract, identical fixed-horizon(12-bar)+10bp-deadband label, HGB fixed-HP, N=5 pre-registered random seeds, canonical TRAIN/VAL/OOS splits. Pre-registered 3-gate design in docs/experiments/eth_candidate_infotime_sampling_ab_20260817.md: Gate A = treatment delivery (kurtosis/dollar-CV normalization), Gate B = OOS skill delta > 2x pooled seed std with VAL/OOS sign agreement, Gate C = cost1 strategy beats max(always_long, always_short, flat) on VAL AND OOS.
prior_lines.reason: Gate A PASSED cleanly (dollar bars: kurtosis 23.8->16.6 TRAIN, 62.7->26.7 VAL, 23.9->12.9 OOS; per-bar dollar CV 1.46->0.54) proving the treatment was delivered, yet Gate B FAILED (decision arm dollar_1x OOS IC +0.0064+-0.0055 vs cal5m +0.0068+-0.0038, delta -0.0004; VAL delta -0.0207 i.e. worse; theta sensitivity non-monotonic: dollar_05x +0.0101, dollar_2x -0.0137 = noise pattern) and Gate C FAILED (all arms lose to always_short free benchmark; dollar_1x cost1 VAL -1.456 / OOS -0.757 vs bench +0.389/+0.344; gross edge per trade VAL -0.68bp, OOS +1.30bp vs 11bp round-trip cost). Since resampling worked mechanically but moved neither skill nor economics, the closure attributes failure to absent directional information in the 1m OHLCV+taker-flow source, not to implementation -- confirming the information-source bottleneck diagnosis of docs/feature_engineering_edge_research_20260817.md.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do NOT retest plain dollar/volume/tick bars on kline-derived data at any resolution. The only pre-registered reopen condition is imbalance/run bars built from true tick data (aggTrades, ~650MB/month via data.binance.vision), which require tick-level signed flow and constitute a qualitatively different hypothesis; even then, expect the same 11bp cost wall that absorbed the +1.3bp gross edge here.

prior_lines.scope: Featurization of the 3-month-old but never-consumed L2 summary columns in orderbook_decision_snapshots (multi-level notional imbalance_{1,5,10,20}, imbalance slope, microprice_edge_bps, spread_bps(+z), log depth z, and snapshot-delta OFI proxies at the ~300s decision cadence) for 5m-1h ETH direction prediction. Pre-registered design docs/experiments/eth_candidate_l2_summary_features_cheap_gate_20260817.md: dense-block splits DEV 2026-05-14..06-22 / MID 06-26..07-13 / CONFIRM 08-02..08-11 (canonical VAL/OOS non-overlap stated), Gate P contamination+coverage-bias audit, Gate B1 pre-designated primary imbalance_5 h=1 IC existence, Gate B2 ridge increment over free benchmarks (lag1_ret, taker_imbalance, obi_1m) with day-block bootstrap CI.
prior_lines.reason: Gate P passed and matters: snapshot cadence is a regular 300s loop (p10-p90 297.6-303.4s), hour-of-day uniform, and downtime is volatility-neutral (covered vs uncovered slot |ret| 10.14 vs 10.16bp) -- so the negative result is NOT attributable to sampling bias. Gate B1 FAILED: imbalance_5 h=1 IC sign-unstable across blocks (DEV -0.0081 / MID +0.0158 / CONFIRM +0.0204), all below the 0.039 detection threshold; h3/h12 likewise. Gate B2 FAILED with negative increment: adding all 12 L2 features to the free-benchmark ridge REDUCED confirm-window predictive rho from +0.0408 to +0.0130 (delta -0.0277, day-block bootstrap CI [-0.060,+0.001]). The only block-stable signal was the free benchmark lag1_ret (short-term reversal, -0.038/-0.076/-0.039) -- the same free-benchmark-absorption pattern as the evidence-signal line. C-lite: composite decile long-short gross +0.41bp/trade vs 11bp round-trip cost.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not retest imbalance/depth summaries at >=5m snapshot cadence for direction. The raw L2 axis (WS-E E1 per-level data, exploratory threshold 2026-09-14) remains OPEN by pre-registration -- OFI literature horizons are seconds-to-minutes and structurally unmeasurable from 300s snapshot deltas, so this closure is not evidence against true OFI. Carry two priors into the raw-L2 design: target horizons <=1min and inject into execution/exit-timing layers, not 5m entry gates; spread_bps_z and ofi_proxy_5 showed non-decisional CONFIRM-only sparks and may be retried as risk/liquidity-state (not direction) context.

prior_lines.scope: ETH single-asset weekly time-series momentum (Liu-Tsyvinski NBER w24877/RFS hhaa113 and Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu JoF DOI:10.1111/jofi.13119 lineage, narrowed to a single-asset own-past-return-sign autocorrelation hypothesis) as a slow directional bias/veto conditioning layer for the 5m system -- NOT a re-test of the already-closed intraday CTA/trend-following axis. Pre-registered design docs/experiments/eth_candidate_weekly_tsmom_bias_cheap_gate_20260817.md: ISO-week close signals mom1/mom2/mom4 (trailing 1/2/4-week cumulative log return) vs next-week return, TRAIN 2024-01-07..2025-08-31 (87wk) / VAL 2025-09-01..2025-12-31 (17wk) / OOS 2026-01-01..2026-02-17 (7wk, price-data-limited), permutation-null IC (rotation-null not applicable to non-cyclical weekly data), daily sub-horizon decay decomposition, and max(always_long,always_short) benchmark backtest betting mom1 sign weekly.
prior_lines.reason: mom2/mom4 sign-flip across splits outright. mom1 weekly IC is nominally sign-consistent (TRAIN +0.113/VAL +0.086/OOS +0.500) but all |z|<1.3 and same-sign-rate is at-or-below coinflip (49%/47%/57%); the finer daily decay decomposition then shows VAL fwd7d IC=-0.250 (z=-2.73, the only |z|>=2 result in the whole test) with OPPOSITE sign from TRAIN's +0.046 -- the familiar single-split-significant-but-sign-reversed pattern. Decisive result is the benchmark backtest: betting mom1 sign weekly beats max(always) by +2663bp on TRAIN but LOSES to it by -3555bp on VAL and -3207bp on OOS, i.e. a clean TRAIN-only pattern that fully reverses out-of-sample.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not retest ETH-alone weekly/monthly TSMOM lookback variants (1/2/4wk already covered, benchmark reversal is unambiguous). The underlying Liu-Tsyvinski/Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen claim is a diversified multi-asset portfolio result -- this closure is scoped to single-asset ETH only and does not contradict that literature. Reopening requires a genuinely different system design (multi-asset momentum portfolio across BTC/ETH/SOL/etc., not a single-asset conditioning layer).

prior_lines.scope: ETH multi-timescale direction-existence screen: the same 5m source resampled to {5m,15m,30m,1h,2h,4h} calendar bars, identical methodology at every scale (model-free AC/VR/sign-persistence, 15-feature Spearman IC with circular-shift permutation nulls, 5-genuinely-random-seed LightGBM next-bar direction probe with the btc_1h_native_swing_entry gate's fixed HPs, and a 10bp-roundtrip benchmark backtest vs max(always_long,always_short) with tau selected on VAL only). Pre-registered doc docs/experiments/eth_candidate_direction_timescale_resample_screen_20260817.md, script scripts/research_eth_direction_timescale_resample_screen_20260817.py, results JSON alongside. Splits TRAIN 2024-01..2025-08 / VAL 2025-09..12 / OOS 2026-01-01..2026-02-28 (source-data-limited, canonical OOS end 03-31 truncated).
prior_lines.reason: All 6 timescales failed the pre-registered economic criterion (OOS net vs max(always): every scale loses by 10,000-24,000bp). Statistical next-bar predictability IS real at 5m/15m/30m (VAL and OOS both AUC>0.5 with bootstrap z>=3; 15m strongest at 0.540/0.536) but its identity is the already-known short-term reversal free benchmark: every passing IC feature has negative sign (ret_1..ret_24, rsi14, taker_ratio), and 15m OOS gross is ~1.2bp/flip -- the same magnitude the infotime-sampling closure measured against ~10bp roundtrip cost. At 1h+ even the statistical signal dies: 1h VAL AUC 0.544 (best of all scales) flips to OOS 0.494 (z=-0.4), the third independent reproduction of the VAL/OOS decorrelation signature after btc_1h_native_swing_entry (VAL 5/5 -> OOS 0/5) and ETH Sigma3-1h (8-seed OOS sign flip); 2h/4h are noise (IC passes 4 and 0). Model-free stats confirm no autocorrelation structure emerges at any bar size (|AC1|<0.07, split-sign-unstable). Verdict: 'direction fails because bars are 5m' is falsified -- larger calendar bars raise per-bar |move| (8.5->28bp median) but AUC dies faster, so no calendar timescale beats costs.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not re-run calendar-bar resampling as a direction fix; the timescale axis is now measured end-to-end with one methodology. The surviving statistical signal at 15m/30m is the free lag-return reversal already indexed by the evidence-signal line -- it is only interesting under maker execution (<2bp effective cost), which is the same conclusion the session-split closure reached; route any revival through a maker-fill study, not through resampling. New information sources (GEX, L2/OFI) are independent axes and unaffected by this closure.
prior_lines.addendum_20260817: User asked whether all ~100+ unified-dataset feature columns (not just the 15 hand-built ones) were checked -- they had not been. Extended re-run (script scripts/research_eth_direction_timescale_resample_screen_fullfeat_20260817.py) added 135 more columns (m7_* meta-model outputs, ai_* signals, cvp_*, regime_*, whale_*, ofi/ofti, hurst, funding_*, etc.) after dropping 29 columns with <95% TRAIN/VAL/OOS coverage (incl. pred_mdjd/conf_mdjd, a discontinued feature with zero OOS coverage since 2026-01-01) and 6 price-trend-contaminated columns (spearman-vs-close >0.5, incl. all m7_*_price absolute levels). 150 features total. Verdict unchanged: all 6 timescales still fail the economic criterion (OOS net loses to max(always) by 830-25,200bp). New finding: TRAIN AUC inflates with feature count as TRAIN sample count falls relative to 150 features (0.695 at 5m -> 1.000/perfect memorization at 4h with only 3654 TRAIN rows), while VAL/OOS AUC stays at the same ~0.52-0.53 level as the 15-feature version at 5m/15m/30m and is statistically indistinguishable from random at 1h/2h/4h (OOS bootstrap z<1.4 at all three, vs the 15-feature version's decisive z=8.6 at 5m). Adding the full feature universe does not unlock generalizable direction skill at any timescale -- it only raises overfitting risk at coarse scales. Caveat noted, not corrective: close_btc (absolute BTC price level, TRAIN spearman-vs-ETH-close 0.26, under the 0.5 disqualifying threshold) recurs as a top-importance feature at most scales -- a known risk pattern for tree splits encoding calendar era rather than genuine signal, though OOS AUC staying at noise level suggests this did not materially distort the verdict.

prior_lines.scope: US spot BTC/ETH ETF daily net flow (Farside Investors public data, BTC 2024-01-11.., ETH 2024-07-23..) as a slow ETH directional bias/conditioning layer. Pre-registered design docs/experiments/eth_candidate_etf_flow_daily_bias_cheap_gate_20260817.md: 1-day-lagged causal flow signal (raw + trailing-20d rolling z-score), contamination check (spearman vs price), 3-split (TRAIN 2024-07-24..2025-08-31 / VAL 2025-09-01..2025-12-31 / OOS 2026-01-01..2026-02-17) x 3 forward horizons (1/3/7d) IC scan with permutation-null, BTC-flow-to-ETH cross-asset secondary arm, and max(always_long,always_short) benchmark backtest across the same 3 holding periods.
prior_lines.reason: Contamination check passed (rho vs price 0.206 ETH / 0.115 BTC, well under 0.5 threshold). IC scan showed a rare 9/9-cell sign-consistent negative correlation (flow up -> forward return down), but permutation-null only cleared |z|>=2 on 1 of 9 cells (VAL h7d, z=-2.13; the matching TRAIN h7d z was only -0.12, a magnitude mismatch typical of a multiple-comparisons artifact). The benchmark backtest was initially run in the wrong (pro-flow) direction and corrected to the contrarian direction implied by the negative IC; even after correction, no holding period (1d/3d/7d) showed all three splits positive against max(always) -- 1d: TRAIN+1537/VAL-57/OOS-1392bp; 3d: TRAIN+10893/VAL+5733/OOS-7083bp (OOS reverses); 7d: TRAIN-4193/VAL-6460/OOS-17895bp (all negative). VAL itself is non-monotonic across horizons (-57 to +5733 to -6460bp), the signature of horizon-grid noise rather than a real decay profile. The single IC-significant cell (VAL h7d) itself lost badly in the backtest (-6460bp), showing scan significance did not translate to P&L. BTC-flow cross-asset arm was sign-inconsistent across splits/horizons from the start, weaker than the ETH-own-flow arm.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not retest the same daily-net-flow-sign/z-score proxy at 1-7 day holds -- the horizon grid already shows non-monotonic noise, not a real signal being under-swept. Reopening requires a qualitatively different hypothesis: (a) ETF flow as a volatility/liquidity risk-state gate rather than a direction signal, or (b) intraday flow-disclosure timing rather than daily-close aggregates. Data acquisition note: WebFetch is blocked (403) on farside.co.uk -- use curl with a browser User-Agent header and parse the raw HTML table manually (repo python env lacks lxml/bs4 for pandas.read_html); exact HTML structure documented in the experiment doc.

prior_lines.scope: Daily USDT+USDC combined circulating-supply net increase (free Coinmetrics community CSVs, raw.githubusercontent.com/coinmetrics/data/master/csv/{usdt,usdc}.csv, SplyCur column) as an ETH directional bias/conditioning layer, a coarser daily-resolution proxy for the causally-usable half (post-issuance CAAR only, pre-issuance CAAR is not forward-usable) of Ante-Fiedler-Strehle (2020 BRL WP11 / FRL 2021, DOI:10.1016/j.frl.2020.101867) full-text-verified 565-event hourly issuance event study. Pre-registered design docs/experiments/eth_candidate_stablecoin_issuance_bias_cheap_gate_20260817.md: 1-day-lagged causal signal (raw + rolling-30d z-score), contamination check, 3-split (TRAIN 2024-08-01..2025-08-31 / VAL 2025-09-01..2025-12-31 / OOS 2026-01-01..2026-02-17) x 3 forward horizons (1/2/3d) x 2 target definitions (raw forward return, paper-style abnormal-return-vs-trailing-baseline) IC scan with permutation-null, and max(always_long,always_short) benchmark backtest across the same 3 holding periods.
prior_lines.reason: Contamination check passed (rho 0.085/-0.014). IC scan across all 36 cells (2 signal variants x 2 target variants x 3 splits x 3 horizons) found ZERO cells clearing permutation-null |z|>=2 -- max observed |z| was 0.83, weaker than even the already-closed ETF-flow line (1/9 cells cleared). The benchmark backtest, betting the direction the paper actually predicts (large issuance -> subsequent positive return, no sign correction needed unlike the TSMOM/ETF closures), lost to max(always) in all 9 cells (3 splits x 3 holding periods) without exception: TRAIN -7360/-14906/-23780bp, VAL -2318/-7898/-12603bp, OOS -2424/-8237/-12603bp for 1/2/3-day holds respectively -- the cleanest, most uniform rejection pattern of the four non-microstructure cheap gates run this session.
prior_lines.retest_guidance: Do not retest the same daily-aggregate-supply-change proxy. This closure tested only a coarse daily approximation of the causally-usable half of the source paper (post-issuance window; the paper's pre-issuance CAAR finding is not forward-usable by construction, so it was excluded from this design, not overlooked). A genuine reopening requires either (a) hourly individual >=M mint-transaction timestamps via free Etherscan token-transfer API (no sender/receiver address labeling needed, unlike the sibling Ante-Fiedler-Strehle transfer-event paper which remains unattempted for cost reasons -- see docs/eth_direction_alpha_non_microstructure_research_20260817.md section 3.4), or (b) per-stablecoin (not USDT+USDC-combined) analysis, since the source paper found large heterogeneity across stablecoins (USDT/PAX/BUSD significant positive pre-issuance CAAR vs HUSD significantly negative vs USDC null) that this combined-supply design cannot distinguish.
